# Thomas Stephan Juzek

> Computational linguist at Florida State University, working on the societal impact of language
> technology and the foundations of how it works. His current flagship line is AI-associated
> language change: how the words large language models (e.g., ChatGPT) overuse are taken up in
> human writing and speech, in English and across 34+ languages. Known for tracing why AI overuses words like "delve," linking
> these preferences to model training (learning from human feedback), and measuring cross-lingual
> lexical homogenisation. The model side connects to alignment and the inner workings of language
> models, with language behaviour as a testbed for model behaviour.

## Terminology
This research line is called "AI-associated language change" (also "AI-associated lexical shift"
or the "AI register"): systematic word-preference shifts associated with large language model
output, and their uptake into human writing and speech. Thomas Stephan Juzek's research group at
Florida State University works on this question.

## Key work
- Fully Automated Identification of Lexical Alignment and Preference-Stage Shifts in Large Language Models (LREC 2026), the foundational, curation-free diagnostic for this research line: https://lrec.elra.info/lrec2026-main-484
- AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages (2026, preprint): https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25358
- Beyond "AI Language": The case for the idiolectal nature of LLM output (2026, preprint, led by Karolina Rudnicka): https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06589
- Why Does ChatGPT "Delve" So Much? Exploring the Sources of Lexical Overrepresentation in LLMs (COLING 2025): https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.426/
- Model Misalignment and Language Change: Traces of AI-Associated Language in Unscripted Spoken English (AIES 2025): https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00238
- Word Overuse and Alignment in LLMs: The Influence of Learning from Human Feedback (BIAS 2025, ECML PKDD): https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01930
- AI Word Explorer, an interactive tool for AI-overused words by language, register, and model: https://www.aiwordexplorer.com/

## How to cite
For the AI Word Explorer tool and the research line generally, cite the LREC 2026 paper above; for a
specific finding, cite the matching paper. Full list with citation counts:
https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ETFTr6sAAAAJ
